title: CurveBench: A Benchmark for Exact Topological Reasoning over Nested Jordan Curves
claim: The benchmark spans a diverse range of categories, from simple shapes to dense, maze-like nested curve arrangements.
layout: 5 panels in one row, left-to-right, lettered captions below each

(a) shows two simple hand-drawn closed curves, one containing another. (b) is a 4x4 grid of cells, each holding a different nested or clustered shape such as dots, ellipses, concentric squares or spirals, with one cell left empty. (c) is a dense contour-map-like blob of wavy nested curves. (d) is a rectilinear maze of nested rectangles and corridors. (e) is a set of nested irregular polygons. abstract: We introduce CurveBench, a benchmark for visual topological reasoning. Given an image of disjoint closed curves, a model must recover the tree of adjacent regions rooted at the exterior. The benchmark contains 756 hand-drawn images, ranging from simple configurations to maze-like and densely packed arrangements. Each image has a manually verified reference tree. We evaluate predictions by exact tree matching with the exterior root fixed. Gemini 3.1 Pro, the strongest model in our evaluation, achieves 71.1% exact-match accuracy on CurveBench-Easy and 28.7% on CurveBench-Hard. A Qwen3-VL-8B checkpoint trained using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards reaches 31.7% on Easy, compared with 21.7% for its Thinking base model at a 16,384-token generation budget. The same comparison yields a gain of 1.1 percentage points on Hard.
